Durban Floods 2022 [6132]

By: Carol Albertyn Christie | Paid

Proposal


Show:

Further information:
Focus of the programme

(John said to focus on the IPCC report.)

As the first drops of rain started to fall in Durban, 1000 scientists from 25 countries around the world staged protests in major centres.

https://www.smithsonianmag.com/smart-news/scientists-stage-worldwide-climate-protests-after-ipcc-report-180979913/

Peter Kalmus who is a NASA scientist chained himself to the JP Morgan Bank building in Los Angeles and said the following.

“I am here because scientists are not being listened to. I am willing to take a risk for this gorgeous plant. We are heading towards a fucking disaster.This is so much bigger than we thought.”

The IPCC Report has said that there must be “rapid, deep and immediate" cuts in carbon dioxide emissions. Global emissions of CO2 would need to peak within 3 years to stave off the worse impacts. That is 2025, on our doorstep or in our case on our coast. Even then the world will need technology to suck CO2 from the air.

This is how I wanted to start my programme. As the scientists were demonstrating Durban experienced one of it’s worse storms in living history.

In April 2022, days of heavy rain across KwaZulu-Natal in southeastern South Africa led to deadly floods. Particularly hard-hit were areas in and around Durban. At least 443 people have been reported dead, and 63 people are still missing. Several thousand homes were damaged or destroyed. Critical infrastructure, including major roads, transportation, communication, and electrical systems, were also impacted by the flooding, and this damage greatly hampered recovery and relief efforts. It is one of the deadliest natural disasters in the country in the 21st century, and the deadliest storm since the 1987 floods.The floods have caused R5.7 billion ($389 million) in infrastructure damage.

Mitigating factors in flood.
Lack of infrastructure maintenance. Storm water drains full and damaged.
Too many people building on flood lines.
Unregulated buildings.
More people in urban areas.
Lack of warning.

Floods in 1987 more rain but less people died.
Areas now with no water or electricity.
Looting.
People protesting because no one has come to help them at their settlements.

I have secured an interviews with;

1.Prof Francois Engelbrecht - Professor of Climatology, Wits University,Global Change Institute,Zoom Interview. Philasanda to shoot second cam

https://www.forbesafrica.com/exclusive/2021/08/17/risk-will-keep-growing-professor-francois-engelbrecht-in-exclusive-interview-on-the-new-ipcc-report-and-worst-case-scenarios-in-southern-africa

Risk will keep growing.
He will lead on from scientists in the beginning and talk about his feelings about scientists protesting.
Can he say that Durban floods direct result of global warming?
Occurrence of these storms on East Coast of Africa indicate that this is a new pattern.
South Africa only responsible for 1% of global CO2 emissions. But our adaptive capacity and existing infrastructure make it more difficult to deal with here.
Impact on climate in SA. CT drought of 2015 - 2017 risk of more droughts is 3 times higher than what it should be.
If climate increase by 3 degrees then maize and cattle industry are likely to collapse in SA.
Increase in floods in SA.
We need to quantify what the risk is and how to plan in future.

2. Ethekwini Mayor Mxolisi Kaunda - I email and they have responded and will give me someone to speak to. I also asked for someone from their Disaster Management Department.

In 2021, a Corruption Watch report indicated that eThekwini was among the top five municipalities in the country plagued by allegations of corruption,
with an estimated 166 cases reported. Here, we need to ensure that we have sound and decisive leaders at the fore. Appointments in municipalities should be based on expertise and experience rather than connections.

(If they can’t keep the shit out of the rivers how are they going to safe guard the city against global warming.)

3. Janet Simpkins - ADOPT A RIVER - They have spearheading clean up events on the beach throughout the year. For 10 weeks before the Easter holidays they have been testing the effluent flowing into the Umgeni. The coli runs into the millions, an indication that the municipality cannot cope with existing infrastructure issues let alone the threat of climate change.

4. Prof Cristina Trois Research Chair in Waste and Climate Change. Former Head of Civil Engineering UKZN. They have been mapping areas before and after the flood and areas most affected. Durban has no proper urban planning. Illegal urban sprawl. No plans how to cope with future storms. Houses built on sand. No proper foundations that is why houses slide down the hill.

5. Imtiaz Suliman - Gift of the Givers.
They have basically done what the municipality should have done. They set up a command centre at Virginia. Sending helicopters out to help with search and rescue. Food hampers.Realising that there were still bodies stuck in the mud they rallied around and brought in search teams from other parts of the country.

6. Palesa Phili - Chief Executive Officer - Durban Chamber of Commerce and Industry

In fact, the Durban Chamber of Commerce has called for the government to undertake a “serious review” of the stormwater drainage system along with the road networks and share their disaster management plans, including infrastructure maintenance and development.

Knock on to Durban business. Trying to claw back after riots and now floods to deal with. Impact on tourism. More looting at container depot. Harbour was closed.

Case studies

1. Donald and Brenda Perry
Their two houses were completely destroyed by a landslide in Umhloti, they lived in one and their daughter and granny in the other. They managed to get out just in time.Granny in hospital now due to shock.
Very dramatic footage of where their house used to be. (Will get Floris editor to do some google earth fly by shots to show what it looked like before.)

2. Catherine and Cameron Ferreira
Lost their bedrooms in Westville. Very dramatic stories of how they were mopping water and then suddenly heard big roar. Mother was knocked down under roof. Couldn’t get out. Her 14 year old son saved her.
She is still in hospital from infection to cut on leg. Great case studies.

3.Residents in Ntuzuma that have lost their house and family. The family pulled out. Too traumatised. Will find someone else.

4. Baby on Beach - Shiraz Mohammed. Hasn’t been in Any newspapers wants R 6000 for shot.
No other publication has used it. Exceptionally powerful. Reminds me of the Ethiopian photo of child and vulture by Kevin Carter.

Carter

Durban Floods Script 10

V/O
It’s eight days after a torrential downpour hit the city of Durban…an informal settlement in Reservoir Hills bears deep scars from the recent floods.
Mac Link
The search and rescue teams have been here for the past 24 hours, they found a man’s body which they are trying to retrieve, there is another team a little further down that is trying to retrieve a little girl’s body that they say was washed down the river. One can’t even begin to think where the families are going to start when a tragedy like this has befallen them.
V/O
The rain started all along the KwaZulu Natal coast on the 8th of April. As the storm developed the South African Weather Service upgraded it to a level 9 warning, a severe event which carries the threat of flooding…the volume of water was so immense that some described it as a “water bomb”.
V/O
Marshall Security’s community leader Andreas Mathios (Ma thay (as in hay) os) defied the elements to warn people.
Andreas
I am here on the beachfront and it is an absolute torrential downpour. The coast is being hit by a massive downpour of rain the weather conditions are starting to change.
V/O
The damage is in the order of billions of rands…roads and bridges - washed away, houses collapsed, hundreds of schools impacted. The harbour was closed and the N2 highway turned into a river, with shipping containers cascading over each other and sliding onto the road…buoyed by the force of the floodwaters.
V/O
Climatologist Professor Francois Engelbrecht heads the Global Change Institute at Wits University.
Francois
“On the 11th of April we recorded 300mm of rain in a 24-hour period over a large area, stretching from Margate in the South to the North of Durban, now that is exceptional. For an April flood event this was most certainly unprecedented.”
V/O
The government declared a state of disaster in the province. 40 000 people were left homeless. At least 435 lives were lost, many families are still looking for missing loved ones.
The police created a Search and Rescue Tactical Centre at Virginia airport. From all over the country volunteers came. Colin Deiner leads the team from the Western Cape.
Mac
Seeing what has happened here can you recall having done this at this scale anywhere else?
Colin
I have attended disasters for about 30 years and this is the worst I have seen in South Africa. I have actually been to the earthquake to the tsunami in 2011 in Japan and some of the sites that we have seen reminded me of that.
Mac
Is it that bad Colin?
Colin
It’s that bad.
V/O
The homes along this river were illegally built and the force of the flood decimated dwellings…tossing cars about like matchboxes.
Mac
What did you hear?
Musi
We heard a lot of rocks tumbling down being pushed by all the water and as the rocks were coming down from the area above us, they were blocking all the water which kept rising higher and they pushed all the houses away.
V/O
For 12 years this had been Musi Ntuli’s home in Reservoir Hills - he is the leader of about 100 families in the valley…57 had their homes damaged. His own was wiped out. He owns nothing more than the clothes on his back.
Musi
Yes, I am lucky my family is safe, even though we did also get pushed down by some water we didn’t drown and we were able to get out in time
Donald
All I heard was screaming get out get out.
Up Sound Grandad
Donald
And as I turned and came upstairs I just saw this horrendous amount of mud coming towards me.
V/O
Donald Perry and his son in law Marchand Meyer had minutes to evacuate their properties in Umhloti.
Marchard
I remember running into the homes shouting everyone has to get out now, grab the kids, grab the dogs. Remember my wife shouting get out and ja.
Mac
Where are the kids at this time? What are they thinking what is going on?
Marchand
My son was still running around in his spiderman suit in the house….ja…crazy.
Mac Link
Durban has a long history of storms and floods dating as far back as the 19th century, the floods this year were caused by torrential rains and a massive storm which authorities have described as one of the worst in this country’s history.
V/O
Although flooding is part of the natural cycle for Kwa-Zulu Natal, Professor Engelbrecht believes global warming intensified the recent weather system.
Francois
If we look at a long term statistics, there is very clear evidence that the number of intense rainfall events are increasing. So the statistics are telling us here a very clear picture of a changing climate system in South Africa.
V/O
Although South Africa committed to reducing carbon emissions under the 2016 Paris Agreement, the government is still actively pursuing a fossil-fueled future.
As the lead author on the United Nation’s Inter-Governmental Panel on Climate Change Professor Engelbrecht says the global temperature has already increased by 1.1 degrees Celsius. At 1.5 degrees Celsius, the impact is permanent.
Francois
We run the risk of initiating the irreversible melting of both the Greenland ice sheet and the Antarctica ice sheet. That means that by the end of the century we will have to deal with a sea-level rise in the order of 1 m and that is enough to displace hundreds of millions of people during the course of this century.
V/O
Acting Ethekwini City Manager Musa Mbhele says the city is following set protocols for extreme weather events.
Musa
We do have a disaster management plan which stipulates exactly what we need to do in terms of disaster situation. So, we followed the provisions of that plan but of course we were overwhelmed.
V/O
Many of Ethekwini’s stormwater drains were blocked and this led to torrents of water that damaged some properties.
Mac
There is a huge issue of storm water drains that aren’t being serviced?
Musa
The issue of the blocking of storm water management infrastructure is really caused by a number of factors but the main one is litter challenge. That is the human behaviour, it doesn’t reflect a bad planning at that level. The solution to that Mac really in my view is to tighten enforcement interventions.
V/O
Donald Perry believes that the municipality should already have revised regulations to accommodate extreme weather events.
The coastal belt consists of hills and sand dune soil and inclines prone to landslides.
Perry admits that this flood was unprecedented but believes the torrent of mud that destroyed his properties resulted from exposed soil above his home.
Perry (New up sound)

We often sit around now, night after night and thanking the man above that we got out and our thoughts are with those that didn’t.
V/O
The Perrys and their 87 year old grandmother got out alive - her home lies in ruins in the canyon.
Musi Ntuli’s Reservoir Hills community wasn’t as lucky.
The city believes the death rate is as high as it is, because of rapid urbanisation… homes built as close as possible to job opportunities. In 1994 Durban had 120 informal settlements. Today, over 550.
Mac
But one of the biggest problems is that people are living where there are flood lines, what is the city doing to prevent that?
Musa Mbhele
So, the solution Mac, we need to go high rise as far as we can.
But that is the only way we can help densify and limit people settling on the river banks and flood plains.
Somebody people were telling me Mac that immediately after the storms that people are starting to rebuild again, because they don’t have an option. But we need to aggressively start to expropriate parcels of land ensure we harness speed of building to give people opportunities to not go back to those places.
V/O
Eight days after being swept away by the storm, the search and rescue team finally frees the body of a man trapped in Musi’s village. With quiet reverence, they give families time to say goodbye. As the body leaves the valley for the last time, a baby wails. The 8-year old girl is still missing.
Mac Lin
These guys are the real super heroes, I guess because nobody else wants to go in there and just hearing the child cry as they retrieved the body, the family walking off, I never be able to describe to anyone what that was like.
Promo
Teaser 1 ( 21 secs)
VO: A deadly toll…at least 435 people dead. More than forty thousand made homeless…many still unaccounted for. Is KZN paying the terrible price for out-of-control climate change.

UPSOUND: I’ve attended for about 30 years and this is the worst I have seen in South Africa.




Teaser 2

KwaZulu Natal…a province with a history of devastating floods. Now hundreds of people are dead and thousands have lost their homes. Is this global warming’s calling card?

The report has documented extensive evidence of climate change already impacting on human beings in almost every single country in the world.



Teaser 3

Durban has a history of floods since the 19th Century, but the rain that fell in a 24-hour period in April broke all other records. Is this climate change’s wake-up call?

V/O The homes along this river were illegally built and the force of the flood decimated dwellings…tossing cars about like matchboxes. Mac What did you hear? Musi We heard a lot of rocks tumbling down being pushed by all the water and as the rocks were coming down from the area above us, they were blocking all the water which kept rising higher and they pushed all the houses away. V/O For 12 years this had been Musi Ntuli’s home in Reservoir Hills - he is the leader of about 100 families in the valley…57 had their homes damaged. His own was wiped out. He owns nothing more than the clothes on his back. Musi Yes, I am lucky my family is safe, even though we did also get pushed down by some water we didn’t drown and we were able to get out in time Donald All I heard was screaming get out get out. Up Sound Grandad Donald And as I turned and came upstairs I just saw this horrendous amount of mud coming towards me. V/O Donald Perry and his son in law Marchand Meyer had minutes to evacuate their properties in Umhloti. Marchard I remember running into the homes shouting everyone has to get out now, grab the kids, grab the dogs. Remember my wife shouting get out and ja. Mac Where are the kids at this time? What are they thinking what is going on? Marchand My son was still running around in his spiderman suit in the house….ja…crazy. Mac Link Durban has a long history of storms and floods dating as far back as the 19th century, the floods this year were caused by torrential rains and a massive storm which authorities have described as one of the worst in this country’s history. V/O Although flooding is part of the natural cycle for Kwa-Zulu Natal, Professor Engelbrecht believes global warming intensified the recent weather system. Francois If we look at a long term statistics, there is very clear evidence that the number of intense rainfall events are increasing. So the statistics are telling us here a very clear picture of a changing climate system in South Africa. V/O Although South Africa committed to reducing carbon emissions under the 2016 Paris Agreement, the government is still actively pursuing a fossil-fueled future. As the lead author on the United Nation’s Inter-Governmental Panel on Climate Change Professor Engelbrecht says the global temperature has already increased by 1.1 degrees Celsius. At 1.5 degrees Celsius, the impact is permanent. Francois We run the risk of initiating the irreversible melting of both the Greenland ice sheet and the Antarctica ice sheet. That means that by the end of the century we will have to deal with a sea-level rise in the order of 1 m and that is enough to displace hundreds of millions of people during the course of this century. V/O Acting Ethekwini City Manager Musa Mbhele says the city is following set protocols for extreme weather events. Musa We do have a disaster management plan which stipulates exactly what we need to do in terms of disaster situation. So, we followed the provisions of that plan but of course we were overwhelmed. V/O Many of Ethekwini’s stormwater drains were blocked and this led to torrents of water that damaged some properties. Mac There is a huge issue of storm water drains that aren’t being serviced? Musa The issue of the blocking of storm water management infrastructure is really caused by a number of factors but the main one is litter challenge. That is the human behaviour, it doesn’t reflect a bad planning at that level. The solution to that Mac really in my view is to tighten enforcement interventions. V/O Donald Perry believes that the municipality should already have revised regulations to accommodate extreme weather events. The coastal belt consists of hills and sand dune soil and inclines prone to landslides. Perry admits that this flood was unprecedented but believes the torrent of mud that destroyed his properties resulted from exposed soil above his home. Perry (New up sound) We often sit around now, night after night and thanking the man above that we got out and our thoughts are with those that didn’t. V/O The Perrys and their 87 year old grandmother got out alive - her home lies in ruins in the canyon. Musi Ntuli’s Reservoir Hills community wasn’t as lucky. The city believes the death rate is as high as it is, because of rapid urbanisation… homes built as close as possible to job opportunities. In 1994 Durban had 120 informal settlements. Today, over 550. Mac But one of the biggest problems is that people are living where there are flood lines, what is the city doing to prevent that? Musa Mbhele So, the solution Mac, we need to go high rise as far as we can. But that is the only way we can help densify and limit people settling on the river banks and flood plains. Somebody people were telling me Mac that immediately after the storms that people are starting to rebuild again, because they don’t have an option. But we need to aggressively start to expropriate parcels of land ensure we harness speed of building to give people opportunities to not go back to those places. V/O Eight days after being swept away by the storm, the search and rescue team finally frees the body of a man trapped in Musi’s village. With quiet reverence, they give families time to say goodbye. As the body leaves the valley for the last time, a baby wails. The 8-year old girl is still missing. Mac Lin These guys are the real super heroes, I guess because nobody else wants to go in there and just hearing the child cry as they retrieved the body, the family walking off, I never be able to describe to anyone what that was like. Promo Teaser 1 ( 21 secs) VO: A deadly toll…at least 435 people dead. More than forty thousand made homeless…many still unaccounted for. Is KZN paying the terrible price for out-of-control climate change. UPSOUND: I’ve attended for about 30 years and this is the worst I have seen in South Africa. Teaser 2 KwaZulu Natal…a province with a history of devastating floods. Now hundreds of people are dead and thousands have lost their homes. Is this global warming’s calling card? The report has documented extensive evidence of climate change already impacting on human beings in almost every single country in the world. Teaser 3 Durban has a history of floods since the 19th Century, but the rain that fell in a 24-hour period in April broke all other records. Is this climate change’s wake-up call?

metadata.Further information: Focus of the programme (John said to focus on the IPCC report.) As the first drops of rain started to fall in Durban, 1000 scientists from 25 countries around the world staged protests in major centres. https://www.smithsonianmag.com/smart-news/scientists-stage-worldwide-climate-protests-after-ipcc-report-180979913/ Peter Kalmus who is a NASA scientist chained himself to the JP Morgan Bank building in Los Angeles and said the following. “I am here because scientists are not being listened to. I am willing to take a risk for this gorgeous plant. We are heading towards a fucking disaster.This is so much bigger than we thought.” The IPCC Report has said that there must be “rapid, deep and immediate" cuts in carbon dioxide emissions. Global emissions of CO2 would need to peak within 3 years to stave off the worse impacts. That is 2025, on our doorstep or in our case on our coast. Even then the world will need technology to suck CO2 from the air. This is how I wanted to start my programme. As the scientists were demonstrating Durban experienced one of it’s worse storms in living history. In April 2022, days of heavy rain across KwaZulu-Natal in southeastern South Africa led to deadly floods. Particularly hard-hit were areas in and around Durban. At least 443 people have been reported dead, and 63 people are still missing. Several thousand homes were damaged or destroyed. Critical infrastructure, including major roads, transportation, communication, and electrical systems, were also impacted by the flooding, and this damage greatly hampered recovery and relief efforts. It is one of the deadliest natural disasters in the country in the 21st century, and the deadliest storm since the 1987 floods.The floods have caused R5.7 billion ($389 million) in infrastructure damage. Mitigating factors in flood. Lack of infrastructure maintenance. Storm water drains full and damaged. Too many people building on flood lines. Unregulated buildings. More people in urban areas. Lack of warning. Floods in 1987 more rain but less people died. Areas now with no water or electricity. Looting. People protesting because no one has come to help them at their settlements. I have secured an interviews with; 1.Prof Francois Engelbrecht - Professor of Climatology, Wits University,Global Change Institute,Zoom Interview. Philasanda to shoot second cam https://www.forbesafrica.com/exclusive/2021/08/17/risk-will-keep-growing-professor-francois-engelbrecht-in-exclusive-interview-on-the-new-ipcc-report-and-worst-case-scenarios-in-southern-africa Risk will keep growing. He will lead on from scientists in the beginning and talk about his feelings about scientists protesting. Can he say that Durban floods direct result of global warming? Occurrence of these storms on East Coast of Africa indicate that this is a new pattern. South Africa only responsible for 1% of global CO2 emissions. But our adaptive capacity and existing infrastructure make it more difficult to deal with here. Impact on climate in SA. CT drought of 2015 - 2017 risk of more droughts is 3 times higher than what it should be. If climate increase by 3 degrees then maize and cattle industry are likely to collapse in SA. Increase in floods in SA. We need to quantify what the risk is and how to plan in future. 2. Ethekwini Mayor Mxolisi Kaunda - I email and they have responded and will give me someone to speak to. I also asked for someone from their Disaster Management Department. In 2021, a Corruption Watch report indicated that eThekwini was among the top five municipalities in the country plagued by allegations of corruption, with an estimated 166 cases reported. Here, we need to ensure that we have sound and decisive leaders at the fore. Appointments in municipalities should be based on expertise and experience rather than connections. (If they can’t keep the shit out of the rivers how are they going to safe guard the city against global warming.) 3. Janet Simpkins - ADOPT A RIVER - They have spearheading clean up events on the beach throughout the year. For 10 weeks before the Easter holidays they have been testing the effluent flowing into the Umgeni. The coli runs into the millions, an indication that the municipality cannot cope with existing infrastructure issues let alone the threat of climate change. 4. Prof Cristina Trois Research Chair in Waste and Climate Change. Former Head of Civil Engineering UKZN. They have been mapping areas before and after the flood and areas most affected. Durban has no proper urban planning. Illegal urban sprawl. No plans how to cope with future storms. Houses built on sand. No proper foundations that is why houses slide down the hill. 5. Imtiaz Suliman - Gift of the Givers. They have basically done what the municipality should have done. They set up a command centre at Virginia. Sending helicopters out to help with search and rescue. Food hampers.Realising that there were still bodies stuck in the mud they rallied around and brought in search teams from other parts of the country. 6. Palesa Phili - Chief Executive Officer - Durban Chamber of Commerce and Industry In fact, the Durban Chamber of Commerce has called for the government to undertake a “serious review” of the stormwater drainage system along with the road networks and share their disaster management plans, including infrastructure maintenance and development. Knock on to Durban business. Trying to claw back after riots and now floods to deal with. Impact on tourism. More looting at container depot. Harbour was closed. Case studies 1. Donald and Brenda Perry Their two houses were completely destroyed by a landslide in Umhloti, they lived in one and their daughter and granny in the other. They managed to get out just in time.Granny in hospital now due to shock. Very dramatic footage of where their house used to be. (Will get Floris editor to do some google earth fly by shots to show what it looked like before.) 2. Catherine and Cameron Ferreira Lost their bedrooms in Westville. Very dramatic stories of how they were mopping water and then suddenly heard big roar. Mother was knocked down under roof. Couldn’t get out. Her 14 year old son saved her. She is still in hospital from infection to cut on leg. Great case studies. 3.Residents in Ntuzuma that have lost their house and family. The family pulled out. Too traumatised. Will find someone else. 4. Baby on Beach - Shiraz Mohammed. Hasn’t been in Any newspapers wants R 6000 for shot. No other publication has used it. Exceptionally powerful. Reminds me of the Ethiopian photo of child and vulture by Kevin Carter. Carter
